text:
jamal: Heads up — we're seeing a big spike in backend qps and 95th latency after the key-normalizer rollout this morning. :rotating_light:
jamal: Hitrate on prefix cache dropped from ~78% to ~32% in the last 5m. Backend requests for seq=0..32 went up ~3x.
maria: ugh, on it. any obvious error logs from cache-proxy?
jamal: proxy logs show a lot of unique cache keys now. Looks like the new tokenizer-normalization changed spacing + unicode normalization. Example: old key 'prompt:v1:\u2764 user:42' vs new 'prompt:v1:❤ user:42' — not matching.
kevin: that token normalization change was supposed to be backwards compatible. Did we flip a flag for canonicalizer at runtime?
jamal: rollout was a config push to cache-proxy cluster 3 (canary then roll). Canary 1->2 were fine, but full roll overlap with a kernel selection change on runtime-hosts may have amplified noise.
leah: infra-bot show metrics: 
infra-bot: cache_hit_rate: 0.32 -> 0.30 over 10m; backend_rps: 420 -> 1280; p95_latency_ms: 120 -> 540.
maria: OK we need emergency mitigations: 1) stop the normalizer rollout 2) enable compat-mode that also accepts old key variants 3) warmup most-frequent prefixes to reduce stampede.
kevin: can we just toggle rollout flag back? deploy-bot, can we rollback cache-proxy config to pre-normalizer?
deploy-bot: rollback can be initiated with `/deploy rollback cache-proxy config 2026-03-18T07:10Z`. Requires 2 approvals.
leah: I'm going to open the rollback PR and ask for approvals in #eng-infra. Also will pre-empt autoscaler so backend doesn't get overloaded.
maria: while rollback is orchestrating, let's mitigate on runtime: enable aggressive prefix merge in runtime (merge similar spans) so batch keys coalesce. Might buy us time.
jamal: attaching a quick profile snippet of a hot path (truncating):
```
# top CPU by function
serve_request  42%   tokenize_and_normalize
cache_lookup   28%   kv_proxy_call (miss)
batch_build    10%   build_batch_keys
```
jamal: confirms CPU spent in normalize/tokenize, and misses blow up kv_proxy_call.
kevin: FYI the kernel update reduced attention kernel latency but increased baseline CPU for small seq reqs. So combined with the normalizer we double-count CPU. We need to separate concerns.
leah: rollback PR merged and deploy started (cache-proxy -> config v1.9). Estimated finish in 2m.
jamal: starting warmup job: sampling 100k recent prefixes and prefetching to cache-proxy. Will run at low qps to avoid thundering herd. Script: `python tools/prefill_cache.py --window 6h --rate 50/s`.
maria: good. Also add a temporary key-compat handler to accept both normalized and legacy keys for 1h. Kevin can you add lightweight diff logic into proxy side?
kevin: adding small shim now, will push with feature flag.
infra-bot: deploy complete: cache-proxy config v1.9 active. Cache hit-rate starting to recover.
jamal: hit-rate now 0.62 and backend_rps down to ~520. p95 latency 180ms.
leah: warmup job reports 85% of top-10k prefixes filled. No error spikes.
maria: excellent. follow-up actions: 1) revert tokenizer normalization change from the runtime branch until we do compatibility testing; 2) implement key normalization compatibility mode in cache-proxy permanently (accept canonical + legacy forms and map to canonical key); 3) add pre-warm hooks to rollout pipeline so any cache-keying change triggers a dry-run warmup; 4) add canary traffic generator that replays recent prefixes to canaries before full roll.
kevin: I'll open a PR for compatibility map + perf test harness (microbench for key lookup cost).
jamal: incident postmortem will include exact timeline and numbers. Preliminary RCA: simultaneous rollout of cache key normalization + kernel change increased the effective miss blast radius; lack of compat fallback and no warmup plan allowed a cache-stampede-like surge.
maria: small note — we should also add a flag in the batcher to delay requesting raw-kv for first N requests for a prefix to allow queued warmup to saturate caches rather than flood kv.
leah: agreed. creating follow-up tickets and assigning owners.
jamal: thanks everyone. Keeping thread open until we verify stable for 2h. :white_check_mark:
